title: Car Controls & Moving Off Safely
whatItIs: Smooth, co-ordinated use of the controls, with a safe routine for starting and moving off.
keyFacts: The biting point is where the clutch plate and flywheel come into firm contact and start to transmit drive.
Push the clutch down before the car stops. Use the footbrake smoothly and progressively.
Coasting (in neutral or clutch down) removes engine braking and lets speed build quickly downhill.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT leave a parked vehicle unattended with the engine running.

keyFacts: The car test always includes moving off at an angle from behind a stationary vehicle.

items.title: Pre-start checks
items.text: Doors, parking brake, seat, steering, seat belt, mirrors.

items.title: Start safely
items.text: Parking brake on; neutral (P or N in an automatic).

items.title: Look, then signal
items.text: Mirrors and blind spots; signal if necessary; final look round.

items.title: Move off smoothly
items.text: Accelerator and clutch together; no rollback on a hill.

a.label: Manual
points: Find the biting point to move off
When parked, a gear helps hold the car

b.label: Automatic
points: When parked, leave the lever in P

onTheTest.question: After stalling at a junction, a pupil restarts the engine while still in gear. Which test heading covers this?
onTheTest.why: DT1 section 11 uses this example under 'Precautions' (a driving fault). Starting in gear so the car enters the road would be serious.

onTheTest.question: Why should a learner understand coasting?
options: It reduces control of the car
It saves fuel on long hills
It is needed for smooth stops
onTheTest.why: Rule 122: coasting removes engine braking, speed builds downhill, footbrake use rises, and steering and gear selection suffer.

traps: Moving off with the parking brake on, or with a left signal still on, is a recorded fault.
Clutch coasting is marked under 'Gears' on the test report.
Never let an automatic 'creep': use the parking brake when needed.

sources.doc: National standard for driving cars and light vans
